apps.description: On-device AI agent for Android, tuned for free OpenRouter/Kilo models with automatic model/key fallback and rate-limit recovery. Tools: web search/fetch over HTTP, bash/Python in Termux (optional headless Chromium + Selenium), Shizuku/rish shell, Accessibility, ebook translation, Documents/Verdroid, Git, crypto market data. No backend.
apps.releaseNotes: ## Verdroid v1.0.70 ### Sub-agents - Your main model can now send out sub-agents to do the legwork, like checking several websites at once. They can run on a cheaper or free model (for example `openrouter/free`), so your main model only pays for the final answer. - New Settings → Sub-agents screen where you pick the preferred model and set limits. - The main agent gives each task only the tools it needs, and never more than you allow in Settings. If it doesn't pick any, the sub-agent just gets web search and web fetch. - Links in sub-agent results are checked against the pages the sub-agent actually opened. Small typos get fixed, and anything else is marked "[unverified]". - Several sub-agents run at the same time and wait and retry when the provider is rate-limited. Sub-agents can't start more sub-agents. ### Profiles - With Profiles off, the in-chat tool settings now say "Reset to Settings" instead of "Reset to profile". - Other profile-only labels are hidden when Profiles are off.

apps.description: Off-grid Android chat and gaming client for the MeshCore LoRa mesh network
apps.releaseNotes:
# Meshi v1.101

Off-grid Android chat and gaming for the MeshCore LoRa mesh network. Connects to a MeshCore node over Bluetooth LE — no internet, no cellular, no infrastructure.

## Downloads

| APK | Signing | Notes |
|-----|---------|-------|
| **app-release.apk** | Release key, R8-minified (~2.5 MB) | Recommended for general use |
| **app-debug.apk** | Debug key (~17 MB) | For troubleshooting; includes debug symbols |

> The two APKs are signed with different keys and share the same application ID. To switch between them on one device, uninstall the existing install first.

Install: enable "install from unknown sources" on your device, then open the APK.

## What's new in 1.101

This release focuses on reliability and release hardening.

### Reliability
- **Automatic send retry** with exponential backoff for transient BLE failures
- **Thread-safe** delivery-confirmation and typing-indicator tracking
- **Input validation** on all data received from the mesh (names, messages, GPS, channels) to guard against malformed packets
- **Advert expiry** — stale node advertisements time out after 30 minutes

### Architecture
- Frame-routing logic extracted into a dedicated `FrameRouter`
- Game-invite and SOS-beacon handling extracted into focused managers
- Centralised tunable constants in `MeshiConfig`

### Release hardening
- R8 code + resource shrinking for release builds (~85% smaller APK)
- On-device-only storage: cloud backup and device-to-device transfer disabled for messages, contacts, and location
- Unit test suite for game logic, input validation, and retry behaviour

## Requirements
- Android 5.0 (API 21) or newer
- A MeshCore-compatible LoRa node reachable over Bluetooth LE

## License

apps.releaseNotes:
# Clint Browser v1.2.3

## What's New

### Tab Groups

You can finally organize your tabs into groups!

- Select some tabs and tap **Group**, then give the group a name and a color. If all the tabs come from the same site, Clint suggests a name for you.
- Each group sits inside a container tinted with its color. Tap the header to collapse or expand it. A collapsed group shows a small stack of its favicons.
- Drop a tab onto another tab to create a group with both of them, or drop it onto a grouped tab to add it to that group.
- Drag a group by its header to move it around. While you drag it, every group collapses so it moves as a single block.
- The header menu has New Tab in Group, Edit Name and Color, Select Tabs in Group, Ungroup, and Close Group.
- A row of group chips sits under the New Tab buttons. Tap a chip to jump straight to that group.
- New tabs opened from a grouped tab join its group. This includes "Open in new tab" and popups.
- When the current tab is in a group, a **Group Bar** shows the group's tabs as favicons so you can switch between them quickly. You can hide it from the tab menu with **Show Group Bar**.
- Groups and their colors are saved and restored after a restart. Incognito groups are never saved, and a group never mixes normal and incognito tabs.

> Tbh, I don't know if I did a good job. All I know is I've never used tab groups before, so I didn't really know what the convenient way to implement it was.

(Thanks to @BunCat09 for suggesting this [#11](https://github.com/jhaiian/ClintGecko/issues/11))

---

### Tab Strip

- Every tab shows its favicon, title, and a close button. Tabs share the available width and scroll sideways when they don't fit.
- Tap `+` at the end to open a new tab. The strip only shows tabs from your current mode, so incognito tabs never appear next to normal ones.
- Groups appear as colored chips before their tabs. Tap a chip to collapse or expand the group, or long-press it to open the tab menu on that group.
- Long-press a tab for Close Tab, Close Other Tabs, and group options.
- Tabs from a non-default profile show a small dot in the profile's color on their favicon.
- Turn it on or off in Settings › Look and feel › Layout › **Tab strip**. It's on by default on tablets and larger screens and off on phones.

(Thanks to @jamestong420 for suggesting this [#6](https://github.com/jhaiian/ClintGecko/issues/6))

---

### Tab Strip and Group Bar Position

Two new settings in Settings › Look and feel › Layout, **Tab Strip Position** and **Tab Group Bar Position**. Each one can follow the search bar (the default), or always stay at the top or bottom of the screen. Both bars can be shown at the same time, and changes apply right away without a restart.

---

### A Better Tab Menu

- Long-press anywhere on a tab card to drag it. You don't need to aim for the small handle anymore. Long-pressing without moving still starts selection mode.
- Swipe a tab sideways to close it.
- Close a tab, a group, a selection, or all your tabs, and an **Undo** button brings them back exactly where they were. Incognito tabs are never kept for undo, for privacy.
- New **search** button that filters your tabs by title or URL.
- New **Show as list** option in the menu that switches to compact rows with the favicon, title, site, and profile. On wide screens, the list uses multiple columns.

(Thanks to Daniel Rioja for suggesting this)

- New **Close duplicate tabs** option. It only shows up when you actually have duplicates, and it keeps the tab you're on.
- Swipe the address bar to open the tab menu, just like Firefox. Swipe down when the address bar is at the top, or up when it's at the bottom. Swiping sideways still switches tabs.

(Thanks to @akshaymaurya26 for suggesting this [#20](https://github.com/jhaiian/ClintGecko/issues/20))

- While dragging a tab, the tab menu now scrolls automatically when you reach the top or bottom.
- The tab menu is lighter and smoother, especially when you have a lot of tabs

apps.description: Free, encrypted internet calls between friends, inside a complete replacement for your phone's Phone and Messages apps. Android, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, Material 3; no ads, no tracking.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's fixed

**A hidden number is announced as an unknown caller.** Some networks attach a placeholder name such as "Anonymous" or "Unknown" to a call from a restricted number, and the app read it out as the caller's name. A call whose number may not be shown now keeps no name: the announcement says "Unknown caller is calling" in your language, and the call screen and notification show "Unknown number".

**One call, one entry in the call log.** When an ARK call reaches the other phone but cannot connect and goes over the carrier instead, the receiving phone used to log both the ARK attempt and the carrier call, and raise a missed-call notification for a call that was still ringing. The ARK entry now waits twenty seconds and is dropped when the same caller rings over the carrier. A missed call that arrives while the app is open is marked seen rather than announced.

Update from 1.28 in place; the APK carries the same signature and your data is kept. Requires Android 8.0 or newer.

apps.description: Android app store for open-source apps on GitHub. Developers publish an app by adding the topic "arkstore" to its repository; the store installs and updates APKs straight from GitHub releases.
apps.releaseNotes:
- **Back up the installed apps**: in the settings, under App backup, the apps installed from outside Google Play are saved as their APK files, with the splits of a bundle, to a folder on the device, on a card or in a cloud service the file picker shows, or to one zip file for moving to another phone or to a service such as Google Drive. A folder stays up to date and copies only what has changed; a zip is written whole each time. The list of apps has the whole page, with a search and the choices all, none or only the apps not from Play. The store's own settings go along
- **Restore** from such a folder or zip file, on this or another device: the page tells of each app whether it is missing, behind, the same, newer, signed with another key or in need of a newer Android, and installs what is chosen one after the other. The sources, bookmarks and settings in the backup can be brought back at the same time
- **Recent backups and restores** in the settings: when, to or from where, how many apps of what size, and how each went
- **Root**: on a rooted device (Magisk, KernelSU or APatch) root can be turned on in the settings. Installs, updates, removals and restores then go through without Android asking. Root is asked for when it is first needed; if it is refused or missing, the usual prompts are used and the settings say so
- **App data in the backup**: with root on, a backup can include the apps' own data, encrypted with a password if one is given. A restore puts the data back only into the app it was taken from, signed with the same key, and only whole: every part is checked before any is put in place, and the old data is kept until all are. Without root, the apps' own data is not part of the backup, since Android does not let a store read it
- **The settings as a page of their own**, with the way back at the top, instead of a sheet pulled up over the list

Download `ARK-Store-1.9.0.apk` below and open it on your phone to install, or update from inside ARK-Store.

apps.description: Android device monitor with a home-screen widget, per-app usage insights and a charging screensaver. Fully offline - no internet permission. GPL-3.0-or-later.
apps.releaseNotes:
## What's changed

- **Privacy log (extended access).** The Apps tab has a PRIVACY band; *Open* shows Android's own record of which apps used the camera, the microphone and the location: when, for how long, from the background or not, app by app and moment by moment. On Android 17, which keeps them, refused requests show too. Shown, never stored; without extended access the band offers Android's own Privacy dashboard instead.
- **System apps page (extended access).** The Apps tab's SYSTEM APPS band leads to every app on the system image, with a search. *Remove* takes a preinstalled app you do not use away from this user only (`pm uninstall --user`); the system image's copy stays and *Restore* brings it back. Every removal is asked about first, the apps the phone depends on say what breaks and want that acknowledged, and the ones it cannot do without (Android's core, the home screen, keyboard, phone app and web view in use, Device Watch itself) cannot be removed from here. The verdict is read again just before the command, and a removal or restore the shell calls done but the package manager contradicts is reported as nothing changed.
- **Kernel page (root): sleep.** The kernel's sleep attempts, what stopped the last one, and the wakeup sources that woke the phone most or held it awake longest.
- **The app no longer appears in its own log.** Every location-flavoured read (cell list, Wi-Fi name and details, service state) now happens only while the app is on screen and goes through one gate, so Device Watch's service no longer leaves refusals in Android's privacy log by the minute.
- **Wi-Fi under a VPN.** The Wi-Fi band, signal, speed, standard and security come from the Wi-Fi network's own capabilities, so a VPN no longer hides or mislabels them; the name is read again when the network changes within the minute.
- **Android 17.** The battery's design capacity from the kernel where Android hides the power profile (through extended access where the phone keeps the file from apps), and whether developer options and USB debugging are on, read through extended access since Android 17 hides the switches.

More in the [FAQ](https://github.com/jrs8205/Device-Watch/blob/main/FAQ.md) and the [privacy policy](https://github.com/jrs8205/Device-Watch/blob/main/PRIVACY.md).

## Installing

Updates cleanly over v1.4.x and later. If you are coming from v1.3.1 or older (package `com.example.modernwidget`), uninstall the old app first — it is a different package and will not update.

**Signing cert SHA-256:** `a787d3be1fa4d58751e246dba9b8f1ded5b6a00ab2675367bf49420928e1a51a`
